how: Kyudo (Japanese archery) dojos such as Meiji Jingu Shiseikan and ward sports centres take beginners; Western-style target archery is not documented here.
Tokyo Goannas (est. 1991) play in the Japan A-League with Japanese and international members, training at Futakotamagawa.
No big walls in the Tokyo plain; real big-wall climbing means the Japanese Alps or abroad.
Needs a purpose-built ice track; none in the Tokyo area (Japan's only track was in Nagano, several hours away).
B-PUMP Tokyo Akihabara is a large bouldering-only gym with beginner routes, a no-reservation trial and shoe rental.
Central Asian horseback game needing a steppe horse culture; not played in Japan.
No camel racing in Japan; found in the Gulf states, Australia and Mongolia.
Samurai Capoeira, founded in Japan, teaches adults and children in Jiyugaoka.

how: Needs working elephants; none are kept for sport in Japan. Played in Nepal, Thailand and India.
Horse Club Ginza offers indoor riding-simulator lessons (walk, trot, canter); real riding is at stables outside the city centre.
Tokyo Tatsumi Ice Arena has a main rink and sub-rink supporting ice hockey alongside figure skating and curling.
Tokyo Tatsumi Ice Arena offers public skating, an ice skating school with one-coin trial sessions and adults-only night skates.
The Kodokan, judo's birthplace, runs a beginner judo school and has at least one English-speaking instructor.
Hilton Tokyo opened outdoor pickleball courts, and other courts in wards such as Koto and Minato are listed.
International clubs such as Tokyo Gaijin RFC play in amateur leagues and welcome foreigners; most clubs train on Sundays at rented pitches.
Miyashita Park's rooftop skatepark has a bowl and stair sets, with a small admission fee and free helmet loan.
Needs a jump hill with snow; none near Tokyo (nearest are in Nagano and Hokkaido).
No natural snow in Tokyo; the nearest snowboarding resorts (e.g. Yuzawa in Niigata) are about 90 minutes away by Shinkansen.
A beginner-friendly taekwondo class run via a Tokyo international meetup group meets in Akihabara.
Tokyo Ultimate holds bi-weekly pickup sessions open to all, plus league play.
Saltwater fishing from the Nishi Nagisa artificial tidal flat at Kasai Rinkai Park; Wakasu Seaside Park rents rods at the breakwater.
No mangroves in the Tokyo area; Japan's mangroves are on Okinawa and the Amami islands.
Needs launch slopes; the nearest sites (e.g. Mt Tsukuba) are roughly 1.5 to 2 hours from Tokyo.
Guided kayak tours on Tokyo's canals and the Sumida River, with a beginner route past Nihonbashi Bridge and Skytree.
Tsuribori Musashinoen in Suginami is a paid fishing pond beside the Zenpukuji river; 2016 source, so status should be rechecked.
Inokashira Park's pond has swan pedal boats, standard pedal boats and rowboats rented by the half hour.
Toda Rowing Course in Saitama (Olympic venue) hosts rowing clubs; Tokyo's Sea Forest Waterway ran a 2022 beginner commemorative regatta but regular public rowing is limited.
PADI shops such as EastDive run Discover Scuba and Open Water courses with indoor pool sessions in Tokyo; open-water dives happen on the Izu Peninsula.
ZAC runs a one-hour beginner Tokyo SUP Experience on the Kyu-Naka River.
Tokyo Bay is sheltered with no ocean swell; the nearest surf breaks are in Shonan (Kanagawa) and Chiba, roughly 1 to 1.5 hours away.
The 85 Club windsurfing school gives beginner lessons at Kemigawa Beach on Tokyo Bay in Chiba, about 30 km away.
No bullfighting in Japan; found in Spain, Portugal and Latin America.
Needs gorges; Canyons Okutama runs tours in west Tokyo about 90 minutes from the centre.
No flooded cave systems near Tokyo; the nearest cave diving is in Okinawa and Shikoku.
Limestone caves such as Nippara Cave are in the Okutama mountains, around 2 hours from central Tokyo.
Needs snow and sled-dog culture; nearest is Hokkaido.
Japan has no accessible glaciers for trekking; nearest alternatives are in the Alps or New Zealand.
FlyStation Japan in Koshigaya, Saitama has a 20 m transparent wind tunnel with first-flight and flight-school plans (2019 source).
Needs a purpose-built track; none in the Tokyo area.
Alpine mountaineering means the Japanese Alps, around 3 hours away; Okutama peaks are hiking terrain.
Tokyo Skydiving Club at Honda Airport in Saitama offers tandem jumps and AFF, about 40 km north of Tokyo (beyond the metro radius).
Needs launch slopes; the nearest schools are around Mt Tsukuba and the Fuji foothills, 1.5 to 2 hours away.
No rodeo tradition in Japan; found in North America, Australia and parts of Latin America.
No free-roaming wildlife to see; nearest equivalent is drive-through safari parks, about 2 hours away.
No dunes near Tokyo; the Tottori Sand Dunes are far to the west.
No natural snow in Tokyo; the nearest ski resorts (e.g. Gala Yuzawa) are about 90 minutes away by Shinkansen.
Volcano boarding is done on Cerro Negro in Nicaragua; no equivalent in Japan.
Rafting needs rapids; the Tama River in Okutama (about 1.5 hours away) and Tone River in Gunma are the nearest.
